title: Separate but Together: Integrating Remote Attestation into TLS
problem: Remote attestation and TLS are typically deployed as separate security mechanisms, requiring distinct verification flows. The challenge is cleanly integrating attestation verification into the TLS handshake without duplicating functionality or degrading performance.
motivation: Unified attestation and TLS integration strengthens security by verifying both connection confidentiality and remote system integrity in a single protocol exchange.
method: The approach extends the TLS handshake protocol to incorporate hardware attestation credentials (likely from TPM or CPU-based attestation). Attestation evidence is transmitted during certificate exchange, allowing clients to verify system integrity alongside TLS certificates through integrated handshake messages.
key_novelty: Integration of remote attestation as a native component of TLS rather than requiring separate out-of-band attestation mechanisms.
contributions: Protocol design for attestation-aware TLS handshake
Implementation of integrated attestation and TLS
Deployment guidelines for attested TLS connections
limitations: Not discussed in title; would require abstract and paper content to assess.
